title: Replay Case — draft 0.1.0
description: Piece 6's fixture format: one executable-control-replay case. A case separates the INPUTS (steps — the calls that drove the machine, with recorded family inputs inlined) from the RECORD (recorded_events — the durable ledger the run produced). Replay recomputes by driving a fresh in-memory machine through the steps and comparing its emitted events against the record — replaying the record directly would catch nothing (the anti-pattern the piece exists to stop: recomputation, not playback). The two verdicts are separate by design (fidelity: recomputed == record; conformance: the record itself passes the ledger's eight rule families) — all four combinations are legal outcomes; the expected block pins the combination. Per the S1 fork ruling, recorded family inputs live HERE (in steps), never in the ledger schema. Provenance: current proposal §8 four modes; the legacy 'replay re-uses the recorded arbitration order, never re-arbitrates' semantics (drift register L5).

steps.description: The inputs: the call sequence that drove the machine. Each step is one structured entry — the four operations never collapse into one generic call.

request.description: Adopt-step payload: the adoption request document (identity/versions/digest/grants/accountability).

grants.description: Dispatch-step payload: the live grant set offered at dispatch time.

recorded_events.description: The record: the durable ledger event stream the original run produced (the ledger document's events array). May be generated by driving a real in-memory machine — fixtures SHOULD be machine-produced, not hand-written.

expected.description: The pinned verdict combination — all four quadrants are legal; this is what makes the double-verdict contract falsifiable.

divergence_at.description: For divergence cases: the EVENT index (0-based) where the recomputation first diverges from the record (or where the two streams fork in length) — the diff must LOCATE, not just detect (falsifiable family b).

then.description: A divergence verdict must LOCATE — a boolean divergence is exactly the anti-pattern the priors forbid (family b).
A match verdict has nothing to locate — carrying a location is authoring noise.
